newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Australian prices head up on low volume.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Australian prices head up on low volume.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board's (AWB) national indicator price hit a high of A$195.00 a tonne fob in the latest week reflecting the response of international markets to world weather concerns.

These were initially based on frost concern in the U.S. but moved to dryness fears in key European Union production regions, including France and parts of Britain, toward the end of the week, the AWB said.

AWB national wheat pools were also revised upward with most old crop pools increasing by A$2.00 a tonne and the 1997/98 national Australian Standard White (ASW) pool estimate increased to A$185.00 a tonne fob.
Domestically, growers appeared to be holding grain until the winter planting break arrived, the AWB said. Trade continued at low volumes, particularly for triticale and wheats for feed.
Milling wheat markets remained very quiet with end users' nearby/medium-term demand satisfied at the present stage, it said.
